correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact published affine sum and all facet constants. After translation by the singleton baseline, every mixed-facet offset is bounded by \(F(R,Q)\), whose normalized density is strictly coordinatewise increasing whenever both arguments are positive. Pure one-direction facets have density \(1/2\), below the full density for \(m,n\ge3\). This yields a strict lower bound on every nonsingleton center-to-facet distance. Singleton facets attain the displayed radius, and summing their ball constraints gives a matching global upper bound and forces the uniform center uniquely.

value.rationale: Constrainahedra are a recent family introduced to encode two-directional collision patterns and support higher-algebraic structures. The Bottman--Poliakova realization has a rich facet system with offsets sensitive to horizontal and vertical run fragmentation. The theorem gives a canonical realization-sensitive metric invariant for the entire genuinely two-directional range, proves uniqueness of the center, and shows a structural collapse: only elementary singleton collisions control the inball while every composite collision is quantitatively separated by a strict density gap.
